overview: Jobs are stored by next_run minute bucket and partition. Each scheduler owns partitions (leased via etcd), polls the current bucket, and pushes due jobs to SQS. Workers ack on completion; visibility timeout handles crashes.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative due load: 1M jobs over one minute.
estimation.result: A one-minute bucket may need multiple leased partitions and many workers.
estimation.implication: Measure due-job skew; bounded queue dispatch protects workers when many jobs share the same boundary.

components.purpose: Identify due work and dispatch bounded batches for distributed job scheduler.
components.rationale: Persist schedule/progress and fence partition or leader ownership so failover does not create uncontrolled duplicate dispatch.

components.purpose: Partition leases so only one scheduler dispatches a job
components.rationale: Use a quorum and fencing; possession of an expired lease must never authorize a stale writer.

components.purpose: Buffer independently retryable asynchronous work for distributed job scheduler.
components.rationale: Consumers acknowledge after durable completion; bound retries and send poison work to a dead-letter path.

components.purpose: At-least-once; handlers must be idempotent; retry with backoff; visibility timeout covers crashes
components.rationale: Assume retries; identify work stably, fence obsolete attempts and commit results before acknowledgement.

entityDetails.purpose: Durable schedule definition and next due time.
accessPatterns: Create/update a schedule; scan due jobs by time bucket or ordered index.
constraints: Lease scheduler partitions or elect one leader; fence stale owners.
relationships: One Job produces many Execution records; edits do not rewrite completed executions.

entityDetails.purpose: One scheduled invocation and its retry state.
accessPatterns: Claim a queued execution; persist completion; retry by execution_id.
constraints: UNIQUE(job_id, scheduled_at) prevents duplicate dispatch records; side effects still need idempotency.
relationships: job_id references Job; (job_id, scheduled_at) identifies one invocation across retries.

apiDetails.rationale: Validate timezone and missed-run policy; execution identity is job_id plus scheduled_at.
Separate the schedule from actual attempts so retries are observable.

flows.title: Register and dispatch a due job

steps.title: Job owners → LB → Job API → Jobs
steps.explanation: Store the schedule, timezone, partition and next_run_at.

steps.title: Scheduler shards → Jobs
steps.explanation: Read the current due bucket and create unique execution records.

steps.title: Scheduler shards → Dispatch queue → Workers → Jobs
steps.explanation: Enqueue executions and persist results before ack.

steps.title: Dispatch queue → Workers → Jobs
steps.explanation: Visibility timeout redelivers the same execution_id. Dedup committed completion and send the same idempotency key to external targets.

failureCases.scenario: A worker crashes after performing the external side effect
failureCases.handling: The visibility timeout redelivers the same execution_id. The target must accept an idempotency key; the scheduler cannot promise exactly-once arbitrary side effects.

alternatives: Use one fenced leader for modest due-job throughput and simpler recovery. Use leased time-bucket partitions for heavier bursts, accepting partition rebalancing and lease complexity.
